Hailiang Education Management Group Co., Ltd. et al. v. Zhejiang Ronghuai Education Group Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition

[Ruling Summary]

In the course of bidding ranking, the act of, without permission, covertly using a competitor's well-known trademark or enterprise name or trade name as a keyword constitutes "covert use." Such conduct subjectively manifests an intent to leverage another's business reputation, and objectively exploits the market recognition and influence of the competitor's well-known trademark or enterprise name or trade name, thereby diverting traffic originally belonging to the competitor to one's own website and gaining a competitive advantage. This method and means of competition not only directly harms the competitor's rights and interests and disrupts the normal order of internet competition, but also damages consumer rights and interests and public interest. It violates the principle of good faith and the standards of commercial morality and should be regulated under Article 2, Paragraph 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China.

The re-applicants Zhejiang Ronghuai Education Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ronghuai Education Group) and Zhuji Ronghuai School (hereinafter collectively referred to as Ronghuai Party) filed an application for retrial with this Court against the civil judgment (2020) Zhe Min Zhong No. 463 rendered by the Zhejiang High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance) in the case concerning a dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition with the re-applicants Hailiang Education Management Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hailiang Education Group), Hailiang Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hailiang Group), Hailiang Primary School, Hailiang Junior Middle School, Hailiang Senior High School, Hailiang Experimental Middle School, Hailiang Foreign Language School, Hailiang Art Middle School, and Zhuji Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School) (the aforementioned nine parties are hereinafter collectively referred to as Hailiang Party). This Court issued a civil ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 1937 on November 29, 2021, granting retrial and taking jurisdiction over the case. This Court formed a collegial panel and held a hearing. Kong Lifang and Xiao Xiaoning, agents ad litem of the re-applicant Ronghuai Education Group, Kong Lifang and Wang Xiaoju, agents ad litem of Zhuji Ronghuai School, and Yang Zhenzhong and Wang Yong, joint agents ad litem of the re-applicant Hailiang Party, appeared before the court. This case is now concluded.

Ronghuai Party's grounds for retrial: 1. The second-instance judgment erred in fact by finding that the "" well-known trademark plaque submitted by Hailiang Party during the first-instance proceedings was not forged; 2. In 2019, Ronghuai Education Group's promotion account did not bid on the keyword "Hailiang," and Zhuji Ronghuai School's account likewise did not set the keyword "Hailiang." The alleged infringing act notarized in the notarial certificate (2019) Zhe Hang Zhi Zheng Zi No. 4542 (hereinafter referred to as Notarial Certificate No. 4542) was not committed by Ronghuai Party, and the second-instance judgment erred in fact; 3. The second-instance judgment found that the acts notarized in Notarial Certificate No. 4542 and Notarial Certificate (2019) Zhe Hang Zhi Zheng Zi No. 4575 (hereinafter referred to as Notarial Certificate No. 4575) simultaneously constituted trademark infringement and unfair competition, which amounts to overlapping protection for the same act and should be corrected; 4. The second-instance judgment ordering Ronghuai Party to publish a statement on its official website and WeChat public account to eliminate the impact of the case lacks legal basis; 5. The second-instance judgment ordering Ronghuai Party to pay Hailiang Party RMB 500,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses lacks basis. In summary, Ronghuai Party applied to this Court for retrial under Article 200, Items 2 and 6 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2017) (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), requesting: 1. Revocation of Items 1, 2, and 3 of the civil judgment (2020) Zhe Min Zhong No. 463 of the Zhejiang High People's Court; 2. Revocation of Items 1, 2, and 3 of the civil judgment (2019) Zhe 06 Min Chu No. 579 of the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court; 3. An order that Hailiang Party bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

Hailiang Party responded: 1. The second-instance judgment was unclear in fact and erroneous in law. The alleged infringers committed long-term, large-scale malicious infringement. The court of second instance, instead of strengthening intellectual property protection, drastically reduced the amount of compensation, which could not even cover basic reasonable expenses, rendering the judgment unjust; 2. Hailiang Party did not request a determination of well-known trademark status, and the first-instance judgment did not address this issue. The court of second instance spent considerable effort verifying the authenticity of the well-known trademark plaque, which violates the principle of determining trademark status only as needed. Accordingly, Hailiang Party requested the dismissal of Ronghuai Party's retrial application.

Hailiang Party's grounds for retrial: 1. The second-instance judgment erred in its determination of the number of keywords involved and in finding that the image text in Notarial Certificate (2019) Zhe Hang Zhi Zheng Zi No. 4417 (hereinafter referred to as Notarial Certificate No. 4417) did not constitute "overt use" of the keywords at issue; 2. Evidence such as page 20 of the appendix to Notarial Certificate No. 4542, page 21 of the appendix to Notarial Certificate No. 4575, and pages 21, 25, 29, 48, 50, 55, and 57 of the appendix to Notarial Certificate No. 4417 all show that Ronghuai Party engaged in "covert use" of keywords such as "Hailiang" and "Hailiang Education" to achieve bidding ranking effects of increased display opportunities and attracting netizen attention. The second-instance judgment's finding that such "covert use" of keywords neither constituted trademark infringement nor unfair competition would lead to severe vicious competition. The "unfair competition acts" regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law do not require "causing confusion" as a constituent element; thus, the aforementioned "covert use" constitutes conduct subject to regulation under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law; 3. The alleged infringing acts continued until after the implementation of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2019 (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law), and the 2019 Trademark Law should apply. The second-instance judgment erred in applying the Trademark Law as amended in 2013; 4. The second-instance judgment drastically reduced the compensation amount without considering reasonable expenses for rights protection, and the discretionary compensation amount lacked basis. In summary, Hailiang Party applied to this Court for retrial under Article 200, Items 2 and 6 of the Civil Procedure Law as amended in 2017, requesting: 1. Revocation of the civil judgment (2020) Zhe Min Zhong No. 463 of the Zhejiang High People's Court; 2. Affirmation of the civil judgment (2019) Zhe 06 Min Chu No. 579 of the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court; 3. An order that Ronghuai Party bear all litigation costs of the first instance, second instance, and retrial.

Ronghuai Party responded: 1. The second-instance judgment's determination of the number of keywords at issue was correct; 2. There was no substantial difference between the keyword backend data obtained by the first and second instance courts from Beijing Qihoo Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qihu Company); 3. The rights status of the images in Notarial Certificate No. 4417 is unclear, and the second-instance judgment's finding that this part did not constitute infringement was correct; 4. The second-instance judgment's finding that the "covert use" of the keywords at issue did not constitute unfair competition was correct; 5. Hailiang Party did not appeal the first-instance court's application of the 2013 Trademark Law, and the second-instance judgment did not err in applying the old or new Trademark Law; 6. The determination of well-known trademark status was a factor in the first-instance judgment's discretionary award of damages; 7. Ronghuai Party did not have subjective intent to infringe; 8. Hailiang Party's claimed expenses for rights protection lacked basis. Accordingly, Ronghuai Party requested this Court to dismiss Hailiang Party's retrial request.

Hailiang Education Group filed a lawsuit with the Zhuji People's Court of Zhejiang Province (hereinafter referred to as Zhuji Court) requesting: 1. An order that Ronghuai Party immediately cease infringing Hailiang Education Group's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Hailiang Education" and cease unfair competition acts (specifically including ceasing the act of setting keywords such as "Hailiang" and "Hailiang Education" in the 360 search engine); 2. An order that Ronghuai Party compensate Hailiang Party for economic losses of RMB 3,000,000 caused by the trademark infringement and unfair competition acts; 3. An order that Ronghuai Party publish an apology statement in a prominent position on its website and on the 360 search engine platform, and publish an apology letter in a national newspaper for 15 consecutive days, to eliminate the impact; 4. An order that Ronghuai Party bear the litigation costs, attorney fees, notarization fees, etc. of RMB 153,000 incurred for rights protection. Thereafter, Hailiang Education Group amended its claims to: 1. An order that Ronghuai Party immediately cease infringing Hailiang Education Group's exclusive rights to the trademarks "Hailiang" and "Hailiang Education," as well as its trade name rights, and cease unfair competition acts (specifically including ceasing the act of setting keywords such as "Hailiang" and "Hailiang Education" in the 360 search engine); 2. An order that Ronghuai Party compensate for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 7,508,000 caused by the trademark infringement and unfair competition acts; 3. An order that Ronghuai Party publish an apology statement in a prominent position on its official website and on the 360 search engine platform (domain: www.so.com), and publish an apology letter in a national newspaper for 15 consecutive days, to eliminate the impact (the specific content to be reviewed by the court); 4. An order that Ronghuai Party bear the case acceptance fee. Because Hailiang Education Group increased its claims, Zhuji Court transferred the case to the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) for trial. During the proceedings before the court of first instance, Hailiang Education Group applied to add Hailiang Group, Hailiang Primary School, Hailiang Junior Middle School, Hailiang Senior High School, Hailiang Experimental Middle School, Hailiang Foreign Language School, Hailiang Art Middle School, and Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School as co-plaintiffs, and the aforementioned entities also applied to participate as co-plaintiffs. The court of first instance added the aforementioned entities to the proceedings. During the first-instance trial, Hailiang Party expressly stated that it no longer requested Ronghuai Party to publish an apology statement on the 360 search engine platform.

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance:

1. Status of the Parties

Hailiang Education Group was established on April 10, 2012, formerly known as Zhejiang Hailiang Education Investment Co., Ltd., with a business scope of education industry investment and management, school enterprise management services, education information consulting (items subject to approval according to law shall be carried out after obtaining approval from relevant departments); Hailiang Group was established on August 9, 1996, with a business scope of real estate development, wholesale and retail of cultural and sports supplies, outward investment, etc.; The seven entities of Hailiang Primary School, Hailiang Junior Middle School, Hailiang Senior High School, Hailiang Experimental Middle School, Hailiang Foreign Language School, Hailiang Art Middle School, and Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School were registered as private non-enterprise units between November 2016 and August 2018, with a business scope of diploma education at different stages such as primary school, junior middle school, and senior high school.

Ronghuai Education Group was established on December 13, 2002, with a registered capital of RMB 50,000,000, and a business scope of: education investment, industrial investment, computer development and application (items subject to approval according to law shall be carried out after obtaining approval from relevant departments); Zhuji Ronghuai School was established on June 10, 2001, with the registration certificate date of the private non-enterprise unit being March 23, 2016, and a business scope of: diploma education at the stages of primary school, junior middle school, and ordinary senior high school.

3. Relevant Facts Regarding the Alleged Infringing Acts

Free shuttle, full-time boarding." Clicking on this search result led to the website http://hjronghuai.com; the fourth search result showed "Zhuji Ronghuai International School consultation hotline: 13989546365 (Teacher Ruan)." On July 24 of the same year, Qihoo 360 Technology Co., Ltd. issued an "Explanation Regarding the Advertising Promotion Activities of Zhuji Ronghuai School and Zhejiang Ronghuai Education Group Co., Ltd. on Our Company's Dianjing Platform" to the Zhuji Court, stating: Zhuji Ronghuai School and Ronghuai Education Group were customers who opened accounts on the Dianjing platform of the company for advertising promotion. Since the Ronghuai parties all signed advertising promotion contracts with agents, the company could not provide the relevant contracts. It provided a disc containing the operation records of the Ronghuai parties modifying search keywords and other information on the Dianjing platform of the company. The disc indicated that the operator with the account 771039345@qq.com, on May 16, 2019, based on the "Ronghuai Recruitment" promotion plan, used 46 keywords containing the word "Hailiang," including Zhuji Hailiang Junior High School, Zhuji Hailiang School, Zhejiang Hailiang Junior High School, Hailiang International School, Hailiang School Recruitment Brochure, Zhuji Hailiang Primary School, Zhuji Hailiang Senior High School, Hailiang Art School, Hailiang Foreign Language School, Hailiang School, Hailiang Education, etc., as the target of operations for keyword promotion on the Dianjing platform; additionally, on May 24, 2018, with the value-added consultant as the operator, using "Zhuji Hailiang School" as a keyword, information on keyword promotion was carried out on the Dianjing platform. Qihoo 360 Technology Co., Ltd. also attached the business license and other qualification materials provided by the Ronghuai parties, showing that www.zjronghuai.com was filed by Ronghuai Education Group, and the website www.xinganjue2.top was owned by Ningbo New Feeling Information Technology Co., Ltd., which entrusted Zhuji Ronghuai School to promote this website on "360 Search."

4. Relevant Facts Regarding the Losses Claimed by the Hailiang Parties

The litigation entrustment agency contract and VAT special invoices provided by the Hailiang parties showed that the attorney fees paid by the plaintiffs for this case were RMB 1.2 million. The plaintiffs claimed that the notarization fees, travel expenses, etc., incurred for the litigation totaled RMB 31,416.83, slightly less than the amounts recorded in the vouchers they provided.

The court of first instance held that Hailiang Group's trademarks: No. 11627294 "Hailiang Education," No. 3362059 "", and No. 29171961 "Hailiang" (hereinafter collectively referred to as the trademarks in question) were within their valid periods and should be protected by law. Through long-term promotion and quality accumulation by Hailiang Group, the above trademarks had gained high popularity in the education service category. In this case, Hailiang Group explicitly licensed the trademarks in question to the other eight plaintiffs and agreed that the licensees of the above trademarks could participate in this lawsuit as plaintiffs. Accordingly, the other eight plaintiffs besides Hailiang Group could jointly assert trademark rights with Hailiang Group as plaintiffs in the first instance. The defendants, without permission, set "Hailiang," "Hailiang Education," etc., as keywords, displaying the above wording in the titles, descriptions, and images of search results. This constituted the use of identical or similar trademarks on similar services. This conduct was likely to cause confusion among service recipients, constituting infringement and causing actual losses to the plaintiffs. The defendants' business scope was similar to that of the plaintiffs, and their geographical location was adjacent. By entering into promotional contracts with agents of Qihoo 360 Technology Co., Ltd., the defendants used 46 keywords involving the "Hailiang" trade name and the corporate names of the plaintiffs in the 360 search engine for educational service promotion. When service recipients searched for information distinguishing the plaintiffs, the trade name appeared in the top positions of search results, even in the title and description of the first search result, and the links appeared on websites owned or managed by the defendants. This violated the principles of fair and honest competition and could easily lead service recipients to mistakenly believe that there was a specific connection between the two, constituting unfair competition. The defendants should bear civil liability to cease the infringement, i.e., cease setting keywords related to the word "Hailiang," such as "Hailiang" and "Hailiang Education," in the 360 search engine for promotional services. Since the infringing acts in this case mainly occurred in the digital realm, and the primary service recipients were online users, ordering that the adverse effects be eliminated online was sufficient to stop the infringement. The court did not support the plaintiffs' claim that the defendants should publish an apology statement. Taking into account the popularity of the trademarks in question, the brand value, the number of keywords containing the word "Hailiang" set by the defendants, and the impact on the plaintiffs' market share, the court, in accordance with the law and based on the actual circumstances of this case, determined the compensation amount to be RMB 3 million, with the two defendants bearing joint and several liability for compensation. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 48, Items 1 and 2 of Article 57, Article 60, and Article 63 of the Trademark Law (as amended in 2013), Articles 2, 6, and 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law), Article 179 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law (as amended in 2017), the court ruled: 1. The Ronghuai parties shall immediately cease setting keywords containing the words "Hailiang" or "Hailiang Education" in the 360 search engine; 2. The Ronghuai parties shall, within thirty days from the effective date of the judgment, jointly compensate the plaintiffs for economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred for protecting rights, totaling RMB 3 million; 3. The Ronghuai parties shall, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, publish a statement on their official website and WeChat public account to eliminate the adverse effects of this case (the content must be reviewed and approved by the court); 4. The other claims of the plaintiffs are dismissed.

The Ronghuai parties, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, requesting: to set aside the first-instance judgment, amend it to dismiss all claims of the Hailiang parties, and that the litigation costs for the first and second instances be borne by the Hailiang parties.

The court of second instance, upon trial, found: The first-instance court summarized the contents involved in Notarial Certificate No. 4417, which was generally accurate, but the fifth search result should have been the fifth search result on the new page that appeared after clicking the link "Recommendations for Hailiang, recommend more quality results for you" on the previous page. The first-instance court did not provide a complete description, which should be corrected; the domain name of the website involved in Notarial Certificate No. 4542, "www.hjronghuaijy.com," was incorrect and should be "www.ronghuaijy.com," and the filing entity of that website was Zhuji Ronghuai Education Consulting Co., Ltd. Furthermore, the first-instance court's statement that the Ronghuai parties set up 46 keywords containing "Hailiang" for promotion was inaccurate. According to the disc data provided by Qihoo 360 Technology Co., Ltd. to the Zhuji Court on July 24, 2019, the account corresponding to the folder named "Ronghuai Group" set up a total of 39 keywords containing "Hailiang" for promotion, with a total of 46 operations involving the above keywords. The above inaccuracies are hereby corrected, and the other facts found by the first-instance court are confirmed.

The court of second instance additionally found: (1) On May 22, 2020, the State Administration for Market Regulation issued a receipt in response to the court's investigation order, stating that in its examination system, there is no record of the three trademarks involved having been recognized as well-known trademarks; (2) On June 13, 2011, the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce, in its ruling No. 10770 (2011), recognized the trademark "Hailiang and design" used on copper rods and copper pipes in Class 6 of the International Classification of Goods and Services as a well-known trademark; (3) On July 6, 2020, Qihoo Company issued a "Supplementary Explanation" in response to this court's investigation order, stating: 1. The advertiser corresponding to the folder named "Ronghuai Group" on the CD is Ronghuai Education Group, and the advertiser corresponding to the folder named "Zhuji Ronghuai R" is Zhuji Ronghuai School. 2. As of June 3, 2020, the consumption data and promotion expenses for keywords related to "Hailiang" in the folder named "Ronghuai Group" are: 401 search impressions, 37 search clicks, and RMB 171.52 in search consumption. The attached CD shows that the display period for keywords related to "Hailiang" was from May 11 to June 22, 2018; (4) On August 28, 2020, Qihoo Company issued a "Circumstances Explanation" to this court, stating: 1. Due to the massive volume of historical keyword data set by the advertiser and the difficulty in system recovery, there was partial data loss in the data CD submitted to Zhuji Court. After technical personnel recovered data from the deep database, the operation records of Ronghuai Education Group modifying search keywords and other information on the company's Dianjing platform are re-exported; details are provided in the CD. 2. The content entered by users in the search box is the search term, and the content set by the advertiser on the Dianjing platform is the keyword. The matching modes for search advertisements are divided into exact match, phrase match, and broad match. The matching mode for search advertisements is set by the advertiser when setting keywords. Among them, the phrase match mode includes an intelligent phrase match mode, which matches based on the relevance of the user's search term to the advertiser's keyword in terms of content, business, and other dimensions. It is possible that the search term does not equal the keyword, or the search term is not included in the keyword. Additionally, errors due to technical reasons such as algorithms cannot be ruled out; (5) The updated CD data sent by Qihoo Company to this court on August 28, 2020 shows that from May 11, 2018 to May 16, 2019, Ronghuai Education Group's account set up a total of 39 keywords containing "Hailiang" for promotion, involving a total of 92 operations on the said keywords. The operation times were mainly concentrated in May 2018 and May 2019, of which "771039345@qq.com" operated 48 times, and "Value-added Consultant" operated 44 times.

The court of second instance held that the issues in dispute in this second instance are: (1) Whether the appellee Hailiang Party has the qualifications as a litigation subject; (2) Whether the appellant Ronghuai Party has implemented the alleged acts; (3) Whether the alleged acts infringe the trademark rights involved; (4) Whether the alleged acts constitute unfair competition; (5) Whether the civil liability determined in the first instance judgment is appropriate, provided that the infringement is established.

(1) Whether the Hailiang Party has the qualifications as a litigation subject

The Hailiang Party's right basis for filing this lawsuit includes both trademark rights and enterprise name rights and interests. First, Hailiang Group, as the owner of the trademarks involved, and the other eight appellees, Hailiang Education Group and its affiliated schools, as trademark licensees, have the right to jointly file a trademark infringement lawsuit. Although Hailiang Education Group did not submit trademark licensing documents when filing the lawsuit, it has fully supplemented the relevant materials during the litigation. The court, having preliminary evidence that the group enjoys rights in its trade name, accepted the case in accordance with the relevant requirements of the case registration system, and later added joint plaintiffs upon the parties' application. This was not improper. Second, the Ronghuai Party argues that Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School was established later than the starting time of the alleged infringement, so it does not have litigation subject qualification. However, the alleged infringement claimed by the Hailiang Party continued after the establishment of Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School. Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School is a subordinate school of Hailiang Education Group and a licensee of the involved trademarks and trade names. The prior goodwill of the "Hailiang" brand also extends to this school, so it has the right to file this lawsuit as one of the right holders. Finally, the enterprise name rights centered on "Hailiang" are the basis for each appellee to file an unfair competition lawsuit. Hailiang Group expressly agreed that the other appellees may use the "Hailiang" trade name, and each appellee, in the course of business or school operation, contributed to the accumulation of goodwill in the "Hailiang" trade name. The parties share the goodwill jointly and may file the lawsuit as co-right holders. The Ronghuai Party's argument that the Hailiang Party should separately file unfair competition lawsuits lacks factual and legal basis and is not consistent with the principle of litigation economy; it is not supported.

(2) Whether the appellant Ronghuai Party has implemented the alleged acts

The alleged acts in this case include both the act of setting keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend of Qihoo Company's Dianjing platform and the act of displaying content containing the characters "Hailiang" on the search result pages. Regarding the alleged backend setting act, the CD data provided by Qihoo Company shows that the operator of the Ronghuai Education Group account was "771039345@qq.com" or "Value-added Consultant". "771039345@qq.com" is the QQ email of Chen Baocheng, an employee of Zhuji Ronghuai School. According to WeChat chat records (evidence 8 from the second instance), it is shown that Chen Baocheng communicated with the 360 platform customer service. This is sufficient to prove that Chen Baocheng implemented the backend setting act. The appellant argues that Chen Baocheng, being unfamiliar with online keyword promotion, had entrusted the 360 platform customer service to set the backend keywords. However, the evidence on record shows that the operators include not only "Value-added Consultant" but also Chen Baocheng's own email account "771039345@qq.com", so it cannot be ruled out that Chen Baocheng implemented the setting act. Even if the setting act was implemented by a third party on commission, the principal should bear the corresponding legal liability.

Regarding the alleged page display act, the promotional content on the search result pages (including link titles, descriptions, images, etc.) also needs to be edited in advance by the relevant subject. Generally, the editing subject is the operator of the promoted website. The involved promoted websites include www.hjronghuai.com, www.xinganjue2.top, and www.ronghuaijy.com. The filing entity of the first website is Zhuji Ronghuai School; the filing entity of the second website is Ningbo New Sensation Information Technology Co., Ltd., which entrusted Zhuji Ronghuai School to conduct keyword promotion on the 360 platform; the filing entity of the third website is Zhuji Ronghuai Education Consulting Co., Ltd. The main content of all three websites is information about the Ronghuai Party's school operation and enrollment.

Based on the above facts, the court of second instance held that the two appellants of the Ronghuai Party jointly implemented the alleged acts. The specific reasons are as follows: First, although the CD data shows that only the account opened by Ronghuai Education Group had set keywords containing "Hailiang", the operator account is the QQ email of Chen Baocheng, an employee of Zhuji Ronghuai School, and the content of the promoted websites involves Zhuji Ronghuai School and prominently displays the words "Ronghuai Education". Second, according to the statements of the Ronghuai Party during the second instance trial and the descriptions of the promoted websites, Zhuji Ronghuai School and Ronghuai Education Group have a subordinate relationship. Third, although the filing entity of www.ronghuaijy.com is Zhuji Ronghuai Education Consulting Co., Ltd., the website content and the "copyright owner" both point to Zhuji Ronghuai School. Although the first instance court's factual determination regarding website www.ronghuaijy.com involved in Notarization No. 4542 was erroneous, it did not affect its conclusion on the entity that implemented the alleged acts. The appellant Ronghuai Party's appeal reason that it did not implement the alleged acts is untenable.

(3) Whether the alleged acts infringe the trademark rights involved

For a mere backend keyword setting act, the alleged mark appears only in the search platform backend as the promoted keyword. If the user's search term matches the promoted keyword identically or in another manner, the promoted website will appear in a priority position on the search result page. If such backend setting act merely makes the promoted website rank higher but does not cause the alleged mark to be displayed on the front-end search result page, then for the relevant public, the alleged mark does not function to identify the source of goods or services. Such "implicit use" does not constitute trademark use as defined by law and does not constitute trademark infringement. For the front-end display act, the alleged mark appears on the search result page and can function to identify the source of goods or services for the relevant public. Such "explicit use" constitutes trademark use and should be regulated by trademark law.

In this case, Notarization No. 4542 shows that on the search result page after searching for "Zhuji Hailiang School Uniform Enrollment Hotline" on www.so.com, the first link title was "Hailiang School Enrollment Brochure - Ronghuai School - Enrollment Hotline: 13806768410", and the description also contained the words "Hailiang School", with the website domain being www.ronghuaijy.com. Notarization No. 4575 shows that on the search result page after entering "Zhuji Hailiang School Uniform Enrollment Hotline" on the 360 browser homepage, the first link title was "Zhuji Hailiang School - Uniform Enrollment Hotline: 15857526328 Director Hu", with the website domain being www.hjronghuai.com. Since the designated scope of use for the three involved trademarks is Class 41 (school) education, teaching, and other services, the appellant, without permission, used the characters "Hailiang" on identical services, which is identical or similar to the three involved trademarks. This is likely to cause the relevant public to confuse the source of services or believe that there is a specific connection with the appellees. In particular, the enrollment hotline in the title would lead parents or students who intended to contact the appellees to the appellant's enrollment personnel, thereby causing loss of enrollment opportunities for the appellees. The above acts violate Article 57(1) and (2) of the Trademark Law and constitute trademark infringement.

The appellee Hailiang Party also claimed that the promotional content on www.hjronghuai.com and www.xinganjue2.top involved in Notarization No. 4417 contained images of a teaching building with the characters "Hailiang". Upon examination, the characters on the images were blurry and difficult to identify, so this fact is not recognized. The first instance judgment's finding that the images displaying "Hailiang" constituted trademark infringement is corrected.

(4) Whether the alleged acts constitute unfair competition

First, according to Article 6 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, business operators shall not, without permission, use another person's enterprise name (including abbreviations, trade names, etc.) with certain influence, causing people to mistakenly believe that it is the other person's goods or that there is a specific connection with the other person. In this case, the trade name "Hailiang" is the most distinctive part of each appellee's enterprise name. Through long-term promotion and use, it has gained high reputation and falls within the "trade name with certain influence" as provided in the above article. The appellant Ronghuai Party, as a competitor in the same industry located in Zhuji City, knowingly aware of the reputation of the "Hailiang" trade name, used the characters "Hailiang" on the relevant search result pages without permission, easily causing the relevant public to confuse the source of services or mistakenly believe that there is a specific connection. This constitutes unfair competition by infringing on another person's enterprise name rights and interests. The Ronghuai Party argues on appeal that the same act cannot simultaneously constitute trademark infringement and unfair competition. However, "Hailiang" is both the appellees' registered trademark or a component of their registered trademark and their trade name. The registered trademark and trade name are two separate rights bases that the appellee Hailiang Party enjoys and asserts. Therefore, the alleged act infringes both the trademark rights involved and the appellees' enterprise name rights and interests. The first instance court's finding in this regard is not improper.

Second, the Hailiang Party argues that the Ronghuai Party purchased a large number of keywords containing "Hailiang". Even if some search result entries shown in the notarizations did not directly display the characters "Hailiang", there is still unfair competition. For example, the appellant's websites were placed in prominent positions with the label "Ad", seizing business opportunities that should have belonged to the appellees. In this regard, the court holds that this type of infringement claimed by the Hailiang Party falls under the aforementioned "implicit use" situation, as seen in Notarization No. 4417. Generally, the promoted website appears in a top position on search results only when the promoted keyword set in the backend matches the search term entered by the user. However, in this case, according to backend data 1 provided by Qihoo Company, in 2019, there was no display volume or click volume for keywords containing "Hailiang" in the Ronghuai Education Group account. This indicates that the search terms containing "Hailiang" entered by the appellee during the infringement notarization did not match the keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend. According to Qihoo Company's explanation, this may be because other promotion keywords were set to intelligent phrase match mode. Therefore, it is difficult to attribute the appearance of the promoted website in a top search position to the appellant's act of setting keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend.

Even if the appellant's websites were placed at the top of search results due to the backend setting of the "Hailiang" keyword, considering the specific facts of this case, it is still insufficient to find the above act constitutes unfair competition. Specifically: 1. Determining whether setting another person's commercial identifier as a keyword in the backend constitutes unfair competition must be judged in light of the specific form presented on the search result page, considering whether the act will cause users to confuse or mistake the source or cause other improper damage to the other person's commercial identifier. 2. From the search ranking in this case, in the promoted links section of the search results, the top two positions were still websites related to the appellees, with the appellant's two websites following. Further down in the natural search results, content such as "Hailiang Building" and "Hailiang Group" (unrelated to Ronghuai) appeared. 3. From the displayed content after searching, the appellant's website promotional content and its own web pages did not contain any words related to "Hailiang". Moreover, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Advertising Law of the PRC and the Interim Measures for the Administration of Internet Advertising, the promoted websites were labeled with the word "Ad". 4. From the perspective of user perception, with the development of the search engine industry and the maturation of its profit model, the phenomenon of paid search ranking has become increasingly known to ordinary internet users. Therefore, even if the appellant's website appeared after entering a search term containing "Hailiang", when the promotional content does not mention "Hailiang", the relevant public will not thereby confuse the source of services or believe there is a connection. Instead, they will make rational comparisons and choices based on the information and services provided by each party. In summary, although the transaction opportunities referred to by the appellees may be an interest protected by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, they are not a legal right. Therefore, whether such interest can be protected depends on whether the alleged act is improper. In this case, although the Ronghuai Party placed its own websites in a prominent position that is easily noticed by users through paid search ranking, it did not hinder the display of the Hailiang Party's information, nor did it cause damage such as confusion or misidentification by the relevant public. Therefore, the above acts of the Ronghuai Party do not constitute unfair competition regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

As for the act of the Ronghuai Party setting the keyword "Hailiang" in the backend in 2018, due to the lack of evidence to prove the specific form of the search result page, it is impossible to further determine whether the alleged act would cause damage such as confusion or misidentification by the relevant public. Therefore, the act cannot be found to constitute unfair competition.

(5) Whether the civil liability determined in the first instance judgment is appropriate

The appellant Ronghuai Party, without permission, used the characters "Hailiang" on the search result pages of the relevant websites, thereby infringing the appellees' trademark rights and enterprise name rights and interests. It shall bear the civil liability of ceasing the infringement, eliminating the adverse effects, and compensating for losses.

Regarding the civil liability of ceasing the infringement, the appellant argues that it has already ceased the infringement and should not be ordered to bear this civil liability. However, the appellant has not provided effective evidence to support this claim, and it is not accepted. Meanwhile, as stated above, the mere act of setting keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend is insufficient to be deemed unfair competition. Therefore, the first instance court's order for the appellant to cease the relevant setting act was inaccurate and should be corrected.

Regarding the civil liability of eliminating adverse effects, the infringement of trademark rights and unfair competition acts committed by the appellant objectively resulted in confusion and misidentification. Considering the high reputation of the involved trademarks and trade names, and the fact that education is a key sector of people's livelihood, the first instance court's order for the appellant to bear the civil liability of eliminating adverse effects was not improper.

Regarding the amount of damages, since the appellee Hailiang Party did not submit evidence to prove its actual losses from the infringement, the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement, or the trademark license fees, the damages should be determined according to the statutory damages method. The Ronghuai Party argues that the statutory damages amount of RMB 3,000,000 determined by the first instance court is too high. In this regard, the court of second instance holds: First, the first instance judgment erroneously cited the content of Article 63(3) of the Trademark Law. The correct content is: "If the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement, the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement, or the trademark license fees are difficult to determine, the people's court shall, based on the circumstances of the infringement, award compensation of not more than RMB 3,000,000." Second, the infringement facts relied upon by the first instance court to determine the compensation amount of RMB 3,000,000 were mainly reflected in the three notarizations involved. However, as mentioned above, the acts involved in Notarization No. 4417 neither infringed the involved trademark rights nor constituted unfair competition. Moreover, during the second instance, Qihoo Company provided backend display volume and click volume data. Therefore, the form of the infringement and the facts of the right holder's damage have changed significantly compared to the first instance judgment, and the compensation amount should be adjusted accordingly. Finally, the court comprehensively considered factors such as the reputation of the involved trademarks and trade names, the nature, duration, and consequences of the infringement, and the reasonable expenses incurred to stop the infringement, and determined the compensation amount to be RMB 500,000.

In summary, the court of second instance held that part of the appellant Rong Huaifang's grounds of appeal were established and should be supported. The facts found in the first-instance judgment were basically clear, but the application of law and substantive disposition were both improper and should be amended. After discussion and decision by the adjudication committee of that court, pursuant to Article 48, Items (1) and (2) of Article 57, and Paragraph (3) of Article 63 of the Trademark Law (as amended in 2013), Article 2, Item (2) of Article 6, and Paragraph (3) of Article 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, Article 179 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Item (2) of the first paragraph of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law (as amended in 2017), the judgment was as follows: 1. Affirm Item 3 of the civil judgment No. (2019) Zhe 06 Min Chu Zi No. 579 of the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province, i.e., that Rong Huaifang shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, publish a statement on its official website and WeChat official account to eliminate the impact of this case (the content shall be subject to review and approval by the court); 2. Amend Item 1 of the civil judgment No. (2019) Zhe 06 Min Chu Zi No. 579 of the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province to read: Rong Huaifang shall immediately cease the alleged trademark infringement and unfair competition acts, i.e., cease using the words containing "Hailiang" in the content of related website promotions on the 360 search results page; 3. Amend Item 2 of the civil judgment No. (2019) Zhe 06 Min Chu Zi No. 579 of the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province to read: Rong Huaifang shall jointly compensate the Hailiang Party for economic losses and reasonable expenses in the amount of RMB 500,000 within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective; 4. Dismiss the other claims of the Hailiang Party.

With respect to the parties' retrial requests and reasons, the disputes between the two parties regarding the facts of this case mainly focus on the following aspects: whether Rong Huaifang is the implementer of the alleged infringing acts in this case, the number of keywords containing "Hailiang" set by Rong Huaifang, and the determination of the fact of "tacit use" of the keywords in question. The above disputed content will be determined together with the evidence on file in the analysis and evaluation section below.

We confirm the remaining facts found in the first-instance and second-instance judgments.

Given that the evidence on file is insufficient to prove that Rong Huaifang has ceased the alleged infringing acts, we apply the Trademark Law and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2019 to hear this case.

We hold that, based on the claims and defenses of the parties, the disputed issues in this case mainly are as follows: (1) Whether Rong Huaifang is the implementer of the alleged infringing acts in this case; (2) The number of keywords containing "Hailiang" set in the promotion account of Ronghuai Education Group; (3) Whether the alleged infringing acts recorded in Notarial Certificate No. 4417 constitute trademark infringement; (4) Whether the second-instance judgment correctly determined that the "tacit use" of the keywords in question did not constitute unfair competition; (5) Whether the second-instance judgment properly determined and allocated the tort liability of the parties in this case. We now analyze and evaluate each of the above disputed issues as follows:

(1) Regarding whether Rong Huaifang is the implementer of the alleged infringing acts in this case

According to the claims and factual reasons of the Hailiang Party, the alleged infringing acts in this case include setting keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend of Qihoo Company's Dianjing platform and displaying content containing "Hailiang" on the search results page. Regarding the backend setting act, based on the facts found by the court of second instance, the operator of the promotion account of Ronghuai Education Group was "771039345@qq.com" or "Value-added Consultant", and "771039345@qq.com" is the QQ email of Chen Baocheng, an employee of Zhuji Ronghuai School. Moreover, according to Evidence 8 (WeChat Chat Records) submitted by Rong Huaifang in the second instance, Chen Baocheng had communicated with the 360 platform customer service regarding the setting of keywords. Therefore, the above evidence is sufficient to prove that Chen Baocheng implemented the backend setting of the keywords in question. Regarding the alleged display act on the page, because the promotional content (including link titles, descriptions, and images) on the search results page also needs to be edited in advance by the relevant entity, the editing entity is usually the operator of the promoted website. Notarial Certificate No. 4542 records the alleged infringing acts involving the website http://ronghuaijy.com, and displays information such as Zhuji Ronghuai School and contact persons Teacher Song and Teacher Xiong. Meanwhile, the promoted websites include www.hjronghuai.com, www.xinganjue2.top, and www.ronghuaijy.com. Although the filing entities of the above three websites are Zhuji Ronghuai School, Ningbo New Sensation Information Technology Co., Ltd., and Zhuji Ronghuai Education Consulting Co., Ltd., respectively, the main content of all three websites is information on the school operations and enrollment of the Ronghuai side. Moreover, the "Copyright Owner" of www.ronghuaijy.com points to Zhuji Ronghuai School. Additionally, according to the statements of the Ronghuai side in court and the content of the promoted website descriptions, there is a subordinate relationship between Zhuji Ronghuai School and Ronghuai Education Group. The above facts show that although only the account opened by Ronghuai Education Group had set keywords containing "Hailiang", the operator account was the QQ email of Chen Baocheng, an employee of Zhuji Ronghuai School, and the content of the promoted websites involved both Zhuji Ronghuai School and bore the words "Ronghuai Education". Therefore, the second-instance judgment's determination that the alleged infringing acts were jointly implemented by Ronghuai Education Group and Zhuji Ronghuai School was consistent with objective reality and was not improper. The corresponding ground for retrial of the Ronghuai side cannot be established, and we do not support it.

(2) Regarding the number of keywords containing "Hailiang" set in the promotion account of Ronghuai Education Group

Upon investigation, the operation record disc provided by Qihoo Company, which records the modification of search keywords and other information by the Ronghuai side on its Dianjing platform, indicates that the operator "771039345@qq.com", on May 16, 2019, pursuant to the promotion plan "Ronghuai Enrollment," operated 46 keywords containing the characters "Hailiang", including Zhuji Hailiang Junior High School, Zhuji Hailiang School, Zhejiang Hailiang Junior High School, Hailiang International School, Hailiang School Enrollment Brochure, Zhuji Hailiang Primary School, Zhuji Hailiang Senior High School, Hailiang Art School, Hailiang Foreign Language School, Hailiang School, Hailiang Education, etc., for keyword promotion on the Dianjing platform. The above 46 keywords were divided into two "promotion groups": "Competitive Products" and "Zhuji Region". Among them, 4 keywords (i.e., "Zhuji Hailiang Primary School, Zhuji Hailiang Junior High School, Zhuji Hailiang Senior High School, Zhuji Hailiang School") were respectively set in the "Competitive Products" promotion group and the "Zhuji Region" promotion group on May 16, 2019. Combined with the introduction of the online promotion business displayed on Qihoo Company's official website, identical keywords can be set in different "promotion groups" to achieve different display and promotion effects. Therefore, in the above promotion account, the keywords respectively divided into the "Competitive Products" and "Zhuji Region" promotion groups have different display and promotion effects, are independent of each other, and the quantity should be calculated separately. Among the above 46 keywords, 3 keywords are actually records of the operator "Value-added Consultant" modifying the matching mode of keywords in the "Zhuji Region" promotion group, and are not separately set keywords. These 3 keywords should be deducted from the total. Therefore, the actual number of keywords containing "Hailiang" set by the Ronghuai side is 43. The second-instance judgment, failing to fully consider the difference in promotion effects of the promotion groups in which the keywords were located, treated the 4 keywords with the same wording respectively divided into the two promotion groups as completely identical keywords and made corresponding deductions, determining that the Ronghuai side set 39 keywords for promotion containing "Hailiang". This was somewhat improper, and we correct it. The ground for retrial of the Hailiang Party on this issue is established, and we support it.

(3) Whether the alleged infringing acts recorded in Notarial Certificate No. 4417 constitute trademark infringement

Figure 21 attached to Notarial Certificate No. 4417 shows that the entry of the third search result contains an image of a building. The Hailiang Party claims that the building in the image is an exterior view of the landmark building of "Hailiang Education", which is a landmark building in Shaoxing City, shaped like an "H", taken from the first letter of "Hailiang". In the middle of the front of the building, four large characters "Hailiang Education" are embedded. The building is highly well-known in Shaoxing City, thus constituting trademark use of "Hailiang". Upon investigation, from the image attached to the notarial certificate, only the outline of the building can be seen, and the characters embedded on the building are blurry and cannot be identified. The trademarks claimed by the Hailiang Party in this case are mainly represented by text, not the appearance of the building. Under these circumstances, the court of second instance determined that this search result was insufficient to prove that the Ronghuai side had made trademark use of the keyword "Hailiang", which was not improper. The corresponding ground for retrial of the Hailiang Party cannot be established, and we do not support it.

(4) Whether the "tacit use" of the keywords in question constitutes unfair competition

1. Regarding the determination of relevant facts

According to the record of Notarial Certificate No. 4417, when searching for the keyword "Hailiang" or "Hailiang Education" on the 360 search engine, the websites http://hjronghuai.com and http://xinganjue2.top appeared at relatively forward positions in the search results, and the content of the websites was all enrollment information of the Ronghuai side. The "Ad" mark was indicated in the lower right corner of the above search results. Regarding the above display results, the court of second instance held that because the backend data provided by Qihoo Company showed that the display volume and click volume of the "Hailiang" keyword in the account of Ronghuai Education Group in 2019 were zero, it indicated that the search terms containing Hailiang entered during the notarization of the infringement did not match the keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend. Therefore, the front-end display results could not be attributed to the backend setting act, and accordingly, the notarial certificate was not admitted.

Upon investigation, the evidence on file shows that among the data on click volume and display volume of the "Hailiang" keyword submitted by Qihoo Company to the court twice, only records from May 11, 2018 to June 22, 2018 were included, and did not include relevant data after June 22, 2018. That is, Qihoo Company did not provide data on the click volume and display volume of the "Hailiang" keyword in the account of Ronghuai Education Group in 2019. Meanwhile, Qihoo Company also explained the possibility of inaccuracies in the information, indicating that its data "does not exclude errors due to technical reasons such as algorithms." We hold that, in the absence of corresponding data for 2019, it cannot be automatically excluded that there is a causal relationship between the backend keyword setting act and the front-end display results. On the contrary, the search results recorded in the notarial certificate show that the "Ad" mark was indicated in the lower right corner of the link of the Ronghuai side's information, meaning that the link was a paid promotion link, not a natural search result. Combined with the fact that the promotion account of Ronghuai Education Group had set dozens of keywords containing "Hailiang" in the backend of the Dianjing platform, and that inputting the search term "Hailiang" could yield the result of the Ronghuai side's promotion link, it is highly possible that the front-end display results were triggered by the backend keyword setting. Accordingly, it can be determined that there is a sufficient causal relationship between the display of the Ronghuai side's promotion link in the above search results and the Ronghuai side's act of setting the "Hailiang" keyword in the backend. The relevant factual determination by the court of second instance was improper, and we correct it.

Furthermore, Figure 20 of Notarial Certificate No. 4542, Figure 21 of Notarial Certificate No. 4575, and Figures 25, 29, 48, 50, 55, 57, etc. of Notarial Certificate No. 4417 show that when searching for keywords such as "Hailiang" and "Hailiang Education" on the 360 search engine, the Ronghuai side's website in question appeared at a forward position on the search results page, and the "Ad" mark was indicated in the lower right corner of the search result, but the keyword "Hailiang" was not directly reflected in the entry of the search result. The above facts indicate that in the notarized contents of Notarial Certificates No. 4417, No. 4542, and No. 4575, there existed "tacit use" of the keywords in question. The court of second instance did not fully determine the above acts, and we correct this.

2. Regarding the application of law

Article 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "This Law is enacted for the purpose of promoting the healthy development of the socialist market economy, encouraging and protecting fair competition, suppressing unfair competition acts, and protecting the lawful rights and interests of business operators and consumers." Article 2 of that Law provides: "Business operators shall, in their production and business activities, follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith, and comply with laws and business ethics. Unfair competition acts as referred to in this Law refer to acts that, in the production and business activities of business operators, violate the provisions of this Law, disrupt the order of market competition, and damage the lawful rights and interests of other business operators or consumers. Business operators as referred to in this Law mean natural persons, legal persons, and other organizations that engage in the production or operation of goods or the provision of services." Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a business operator disrupts the order of market competition, damages the lawful rights and interests of other business operators or consumers, and the act falls outside the circumstances provided for in Chapter II of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and the Patent Law, Trademark Law, Copyright Law, etc., the people's court may apply Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to determine it."

We hold that, in the context of promoting socialist core values, to achieve the healthy development of the market economy, the freedom of competition and innovation of market entities should be based on following the principle of good faith and complying with business ethics. With the rapid development of the internet industry, unfair competition acts in the internet field emerge one after another. The specific acts of unfair competition enumerated in Articles 6 to 12 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law can no longer cover all unfair competition acts that exist in reality. Whether a competitive act in the internet field is improper shall be determined by considering the nature and characteristics of the specific business model in the internet economic environment, judging the subjective state of the actor, and comprehensively considering the impact of the act on the interests of business operators, consumer rights and interests, the market competition order, and social public interests. The determination shall be made based on whether it violates the principle of good faith and business ethics.

In this case, in the process of internet bidding ranking, the Ronghuai side set as keywords the words containing the "Hailiang" trademark or enterprise name of its competitor, the Hailiang Party, for "tacit use." The second-instance judgment held that the above act of the Ronghuai side did not hinder the display of the Hailiang Party's website, nor did it cause consumer confusion or misidentification, and did not cause damage. Therefore, the above act of the Ronghuai side constituted neither trademark infringement nor unfair competition. The Hailiang Party claims that the "tacit use" act constitutes unfair competition, and the second-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly.

Regarding this, we hold as follows: First, we should analyze the subjective intent, results, and causal relationship of the Ronghuai side's implementation of the alleged infringing acts in light of the nature and characteristics of the bidding ranking business model. Bidding ranking is a commercial act in which merchants promoting products or services purchase promotion services from search engines, independently select a certain number of keywords to set in the backend of the search engine to promote their own websites. Under the bidding ranking business model, if multiple entities purchase the same keyword, the one with the higher bid generally ranks higher in the search results. The higher the popularity of the selected keyword in the minds of consumers, the higher the matching degree between the keyword and the consumer's input search term, and the more likely the merchant's promotion link can "stand out" from the vast amount of internet information, thereby achieving the advertising effect of publicity and promotion. In this case, based on the evidence provided by the Hailiang Party, the "Hailiang" trademark and the "Hailiang" enterprise name for which rights are claimed have strong distinctiveness and enjoy high visibility and influence in services such as education and training. Such visibility and influence are the market achievements and goodwill accumulated by the Hailiang Group and its affiliated schools through long-term use and extensive publicity, and should be protected by law. The Ronghuai side, as a competitor in the same geographic region as the Hailiang Party, should obviously be aware of the visibility and influence of the "Hailiang" brand. However, in the bidding ranking process, it not only failed to avoid "Hailiang" but instead set the names of multiple schools of the Hailiang Party as keywords in the backend of the search engine. Its subjective intent was to take advantage of the goodwill of "Hailiang", and its intention to use the visibility of "Hailiang" to attract consumers' attention to its own education brand was very clear. Although the title of the Ronghuai side's promoted link and the content displayed on the target website of the link did not contain any identifiers or promotional content related to "Hailiang", and seemed unlikely to cause consumer confusion or misidentification, from the perspective of the consequences of the alleged infringing acts, because the Ronghuai side had set multiple keywords containing "Hailiang" in the search engine, when a network user searched for "Hailiang", it would trigger the Ronghuai side's paid promotion link, causing the promotion link to appear at a relatively forward position in the search results. That is, regardless of whether the keyword "Hailiang" was directly reflected in the entry of the search result, it does not affect the Ronghuai side's use of the visibility of "Hailiang" to achieve the goal of promoting and publicizing its own target website.

Second, creating a fair competition market order is an inherent requirement for promoting the healthy development of the socialist market economy. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law encourages freedom of competition and freedom of innovation, but freedom of competition and freedom of innovation must not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of others, nor damage social public interests. Only by encouraging and supporting the accumulation of social wealth and creation of social value through honest labor, and protecting the lawful property interests formed on this basis, while advocating that business operators act with integrity and honesty in market activities, pursuing their own interests without harming the lawful interests of others, social public interests, and the market order, can we create a good environment and conditions for fair competition, thereby stimulating the innovation vitality and motivation of market entities. In this case, the alleged infringing acts of the Ronghuai side occurred in the internet field. Whether they caused damage should also be considered in the context of the internet economy, from the following aspects:

First, the internet is a virtual platform built on digital technology. Under the internet business model, consumer attention and traffic are closely related to commercial interests and have become the target and core resource of commercial competition in the internet field. Diverting the traffic of others will inevitably harm the commercial interests of others. Therefore, when assessing the consequences of damage caused by infringing acts under the internet business model, the above characteristics of internet commercial competition should be fully considered. The purpose of merchants engaging in paid ranking is to achieve the effect of display and promotion through keywords, rather than to cause confusion with others. Moreover, "unfair competition acts" regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law do not require "causing confusion or misidentification" as a constituent element. Acts that violate the principle of good faith and business ethics also constitute unfair competition, even if they do not cause consumer confusion or misidentification. In this case, Ronghuai's "hidden use" of the keyword "Hailiang" was precisely to attract traffic originally belonging to Hailiang to its own website by utilizing the popularity and influence of "Hailiang" in the minds of consumers, as well as the concealment characteristic of keyword setting. This increased the exposure of its own website, thereby gaining a competitive advantage, and also caused damage to Hailiang's competitive interests.

Second, the essence of market competition is the contest for transaction opportunities or competitive advantages. In competition, damage to the interests of one party is inevitable. Therefore, even if a competitive act causes competitive damage, it does not necessarily mean that the act is inherently improper. Whether a competitive act is proper also needs to be comprehensively evaluated by considering its impact on the market competition order, consumer rights and interests, and the interests of other market entities. In this case, in order to gain a competitive advantage, Ronghuai did not operate in good faith or strive to improve the quality or reputation of its own brand. Instead, it adopted the method of "hidden use" by setting its competitor Hailiang's well-known trademark or enterprise name as a keyword to promote its own brand. This way of participating in competition should not be encouraged or promoted. If Ronghuai's "hidden use" of the keyword in question is not regulated, not only would Hailiang's long-term accumulated market achievements be left unprotected, but it would also inevitably dampen the enthusiasm of other market entities to operate in good faith, thereby suppressing market vitality. It is particularly important to point out that, for paid ranking, whether Ronghuai used the keyword "Hailiang" in a "visible use" or "hidden use" manner, the objective promotional effect is the same, and this promotional effect was obtained through the market popularity of Hailiang's "Hailiang" brand. Under these circumstances, the conclusion of the second-instance judgment that "visible use" of the keyword in question constituted infringement while "hidden use" of the keyword did not would inevitably create a negative guidance for market entities on the competitive methods and means to be adopted in the process of paid ranking, which is not conducive to creating a fair competition market environment.

Third, the paid ranking business model involved in the alleged infringing act in this case is a commercial promotion service based on search engines. Search engines carry the basic function of providing network users with search results that have the greatest degree of relevance to their query content, and thus have a certain public interest nature. Network users who use search engines to retrieve information usually have specific goals and needs, and the purpose of search engine services is to reduce the cost of information retrieval and improve the efficiency of information retrieval. According to the evidence on record, when a network user uses a search engine to search for "Hailiang," the search results display not only Hailiang's related websites but also Ronghuai's paid promotion links, and some of the promoted links appear in relatively forward positions in the search results. At this point, the relevant network user needs to further identify the relevance between the search result and the search term in order to obtain the needed information. Therefore, Ronghuai's above "hidden use" of the keyword "Hailiang" caused information interference to network users, increased search costs, and also hindered the normal functioning of the basic functions of the search engine.

Fourth, consumers' right to obtain information is only one aspect of consumer rights and interests. The ability of consumers to obtain rich and extensive information through search engines depends on search engines continuously optimizing algorithms, improving matching modes, and other technical means. Satisfying consumers' needs for information acquisition should not come at the expense of damaging the legitimate rights and interests of market entities or undermining the order of fair competition. Otherwise, it will cause greater damage to consumer rights and interests.

In summary, the essence of paid ranking is a commercial act. Merchants purchasing keywords for paid ranking must be regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. They cannot seize others' transaction opportunities or seek improper benefits by means that violate the principle of good faith and business ethics. Ronghuai's act of setting others' commercial identifiers as keywords for "hidden use" in paid ranking violates the principle of good faith and business ethics. It not only infringes upon Hailiang's legitimate rights and interests and disrupts the normal internet competition order, but also damages consumer rights and interests and social public interests. It constitutes an unfair competition act as stipulated in paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and should be regulated in accordance with the above legal provisions. The second-instance judgment contained errors in both the factual findings and legal application on this issue, and this Court hereby corrects them.

(5) Regarding the Determination and Allocation of Tort Liability of the Parties to this Case

1. Determination of Tort Liability. In this case, "Hailiang" is not only a registered trademark of Hailiang or a component thereof, but also its trade name. Hailiang enjoys exclusive rights to its registered trademark and rights to its enterprise name in accordance with the law. Because Ronghuai's "visible use" of the keyword "Hailiang" infringed upon the trademark rights at issue and also infringed upon Hailiang's enterprise name rights and trade name, Hailiang also filed claims under the relevant provisions of the Trademark Law and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Therefore, the second-instance court's determination that Ronghuai constituted both trademark infringement and unfair competition and should bear corresponding tort liability was factually and legally justified and not improper. Furthermore, Ronghuai's act of "hidden use" of the keyword also should bear corresponding tort liability. Ronghuai's corresponding retrial application grounds cannot be established, and this Court does not support them.

2. Method of Bearing Liability in this Case. Article 179 of the Civil Code of the PRC stipulates that the methods of bearing civil liability include cessation of infringement, removal of obstacles, elimination of danger, compensation for losses, apology, and elimination of adverse effects, among others. This Court holds that, given that the trademark infringement and unfair competition acts committed by Ronghuai objectively resulted in confusion and misidentification, and considering factors such as the high popularity of the trademark and trade name in question and that education is a key livelihood industry, Ronghuai should bear the civil liability of eliminating the adverse effects in this case.

3. Amount of Compensation. Article 63, paragraph 3, of the Trademark Law provides: "Where the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to infringement, the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement, or the royalty for the licensed use of the registered trademark are difficult to determine, the people's court shall award compensation of not more than RMB 5,000,000 based on the circumstances of the infringement." Article 17, paragraph 3, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "The amount of compensation for a business operator harmed by an act of unfair competition shall be determined according to the actual losses suffered by the business operator due to the infringement; where the actual losses are difficult to calculate, the amount shall be determined according to the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement. Where a business operator maliciously commits an act of infringing trade secrets, and the circumstances are serious, the amount of compensation may be determined within a range of one to five times the amount determined by the above methods. The amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses paid by the business operator to stop the infringement." Paragraph 4 of the same article provides: "Where a business operator violates Article 6 or Article 9 of this Law, and the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to infringement or the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement are difficult to determine, the people's court shall award compensation of not more than RMB 5,000,000 to the right holder based on the circumstances of the infringement."

In this case, Hailiang did not provide evidence to prove its actual losses suffered due to the infringement or the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement, and requested that the compensation be determined by statutory damages. This Court, taking into comprehensive consideration the popularity of the trademark and trade name in question, the circumstances and consequences of the infringement, Hailiang's expenses in enforcing its rights, and the errors in the second-instance court's findings of facts related to this case (including the number of keywords and the facts concerning the alleged infringement involved in the Notarial Deeds No. 4417, No. 4542, and No. 4575), and other factors, hereby determines the amount of compensation in this case to be RMB 2,600,000. Ronghuai's corresponding retrial application grounds concerning the amount of compensation cannot be established, and this Court does not support them. Hailiang's corresponding retrial application grounds concerning the amount of compensation are partially established, and this Court supports them.

Additionally, Ronghuai also argued that the second-instance court erroneously found that the well-known trademark plaque submitted by Hailiang was not forged. Upon review, Hailiang clearly stated that it did not request a determination of a well-known trademark, and the second-instance court did not protect the trademark at issue as a well-known trademark. Therefore, whether the well-known trademark plaque was forged has no substantive impact on the determination of the alleged infringement or the outcome of the judgment. Ronghuai's corresponding retrial application grounds cannot be established, and this Court does not support them.

In conclusion, the retrial applications of the retrial applicants, Hailiang Education Group, Hailiang Group, Hailiang Primary School, Hailiang Junior High School, Hailiang Senior High School, Hailiang Experimental Middle School, Hailiang Foreign Language School, Hailiang Art Middle School, and Hailiang Foreign Language Middle School, are partially established, and this Court supports them. The retrial application of the retrial applicant Ronghuai Education Group and Zhuji Ronghuai School lacks sufficient factual and legal basis, and this Court hereby dismisses it in accordance with the law. The first-instance and second-instance judgments both contained errors in fact-finding and application of law, and this Court hereby corrects them. Pursuant to Article 179 of the Civil Code of the PRC, Articles 48, 57(1) and (2), and 63(3) of the Trademark Law of the PRC, Articles 1, 2, 6(2), 17(3) and (4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC, Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC, and Article 177(1)(2) and 214(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

2. The civil judgment (2019) Zhe 06 Min Chu No. 579 of the Shaoxing Intermediate People's Court, Zhejiang Province, is hereby reversed.

3. Zhejiang Ronghuai Education Group Co., Ltd. and Zhuji Ronghuai School shall immediately cease the trademark infringement and unfair competition acts at issue, that is, cease setting keywords containing the words "Hailiang" or "Hailiang Education" in the 360 search engine, and cease using content containing the words "Hailiang" in the promoted content of relevant websites on the 360 search results page.

4. Zhejiang Ronghuai Education Group Co., Ltd. and Zhuji Ronghuai School shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, publish a statement on their official website and WeChat public account to eliminate the adverse effects of this case (the content shall be subject to review and approval by the court).
